answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before it can influence shared decisions; a randomly selected set of peers checks its signed actions against later evidence, and proven fraud burns the bond. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not create free influence: every account needs separately locked funds, while coordinated accounts risk all being exposed by one audit. A whisper from an island can cross the bridge, but it cannot bypass the bond, so the attacker pays capital and risks losing it for each Sybil.
